title: Does a framing nailer's recoil knock a stock Unitree G1 arm off the stud window?
summary: A closed-loop MuJoCo check on the Menagerie G1 holding a 3.4 kg nailer against a wall (pelvis fixed, no legs). A half-sine recoil impulse hits the tip; the sweep covers impulse (0.25–8 N s), loop bandwidth (2–12 Hz), delay (0–20 ms), wall stiffness and preload. Up to 4 N s the tip stays within 1–4 mm of its place (joint-nail window ±3.9 mm) for 4–12 Hz loops, but an impulse of 1 N s or more lifts the nosepiece off the wall for 25–140 ms, and stiff loops go unstable with 10–20 ms of delay. The recoil of a real nailer, the G1's loop delay, the wall stiffness and damping, and the 4 ms pulse are not sourced (swept or assumed); legs and balance are not modelled.
lede: does a framing nailer's recoil knock a stock Unitree G1 arm off the stud window? In a closed-loop MuJoCo hold, up to 4 N s of recoil moves the tip 1-4 mm (window +-3.9 mm) but 1 N s or more lifts the nosepiece off the wall for 25-140 ms; stiff loops go unstable with 10-20 ms delay (recoil, delay and wall are swept, not sourced).
